title: FastDyn: High-Throughput Dynamic Binary Analysis via Adaptive QEMU Execution Slicing
authors: Alex Chen, Elena Rostova, Marcus Johnson, Lab Director
abstract: Dynamic binary analysis is foundational for malware triaging, vulnerability discovery, and taint tracking, yet existing DBI engines incur prohibitive performance penalties (10x-50x overhead). We present FastDyn, a next-generation dynamic execution engine integrated into QEMU that selectively optimizes intermediate code translation blocks through lightweight hardware-assisted checkpoints. FastDyn achieves near-native fuzzing and analysis throughput while retaining instruction-level inspection fidelity.

title: Breaking the Nervous System: Automated Protocol Fuzzing and Semantic State Verification for Robot Middleware DDS
authors: Sarah Miller, Priya Patel, Alex Chen, Lab Director
abstract: Data Distribution Service (DDS) is the standardized communication backbone for critical cyber-physical systems, autonomous vehicles, and ROS2-based robotic deployments. We introduce ddsfuzz, a semantics-aware differential protocol fuzzer that systematically synthesizes stateful message sequences, models QoS policies, and detects desynchronization attacks and memory-corruption vulnerabilities. We evaluated ddsfuzz against the top four open-source DDS implementations, discovering 19 zero-day CVEs.

title: Accelerating Directed Memory-Bug Fuzzing via LLVM Bitcode Dependency Slicing
authors: Elena Rostova, David K. Zhang, Lab Director
abstract: Directed greybox fuzzing aims to trigger specific dangerous target locations (such as unpatched vulnerabilities or sanitization warnings), but spends substantial cycles executing irrelevant program trajectories. We propose Slicer, an automated bitcode-level program slicing framework for LLVM that constructs lean, semantics-preserving target slices and fast-path execution paths. Slicer outperforms state-of-the-art directed fuzzers by up to 14.8x in time-to-exposure for critical zero-day vulnerabilities.

title: xbin: A Unified Heterogeneous Backend Orchestration Framework for Large-Scale Binary Triage
authors: David K. Zhang, Marcus Johnson, Kevin Vance, Lab Director
abstract: Security practitioners routinely struggle to combine disjoint binary analysis frameworks (Ghidra, IDA Pro, angr, Binary Ninja, BAP) due to divergent intermediate representations (IR) and execution models. We present xbin, a unified multi-backend orchestration pipeline that exposes a normalized cross-architecture AST, enabling seamless cross-tool verification, semantic diffing, and automated gadget extraction across stripped binaries.

title: Pieces: Fine-Grained Firmware Decomposition and Transformation for Heterogeneous Embedded MCUs
authors: Kevin Vance, Alex Chen, Linnea Holmgren, Lab Director
abstract: Monolithic microcontroller (MCU) firmware blobs lack standard OS abstractions, making binary instrumentation, debloating, and memory isolation notoriously difficult. Pieces introduces automated firmware reconstruction techniques that disassemble raw blobs, recover symbol tables and MMIO peripheries, and weave fine-grained compartmentalization boundaries into IoT firmware without source code.

title: Confidential Compartments: Zero-Trust Hardware Enclave Isolation for Cloud-Native Microservices
authors: David K. Zhang, Linnea Holmgren, Lab Director
abstract: Hardware-enforced confidential computing environments (such as AMD SEV-SNP and Intel TDX) guarantee memory confidentiality against untrusted cloud hypervisors. However, intra-enclave privilege escalation and side-channel leakage remain major risks. We design a zero-trust compartmentalization architecture that enforces sub-millisecond memory protection domains within virtual machine enclaves.
